zh.summary: 分清漏洞編號、缺陷類型與產品名稱，以版本、設定及修補證據判斷掃描警告。

sourceBody.text: 這一課將幫助你在辨認資安名詞後，進一步理解當弱點掃描工具告訴你「系統有漏洞」時，你要如何判斷這個警告是不是真的。
先記住一個觀念：
掃描器說你的系統「可能有漏洞」，不代表系統真的存在該漏洞；即使確認有漏洞，也不代表駭客已經入侵。
一、用汽車召回事件，一次搞懂三個名詞
假設你買了一台 Toyota 汽車。
某天新聞報導：「某款 Toyota 汽車的煞車系統存在安全缺陷，車廠宣布召回。」
這時候你會想知道：

items: 這次是哪一件召回事件？
煞車究竟是哪一類問題？
我的車型和年份是否也有問題？

sourceBody.text: 資訊安全領域剛好有三套對應的標準。

rows: 某一個公開漏洞的編號
煞車設計或製造錯誤的類型
軟體、硬體或作業系統的標準化產品名稱

visual.caption: 圖 1｜CVE、CWE、CPE 與現場證據
visual.description: 三種平行觀察角度共同支援設備適用性判斷。

items.title: CVE
items.body: 發生哪個漏洞？

items.title: CWE
items.body: 缺陷屬於哪一類？

items.title: CPE
items.body: 可能影響什麼產品？

items.title: 對照版本、設定、修補與現場證據
items.body: 由三個觀察角度核對實際條件

items.title: 這台實際設備到底有沒有受到影響？
items.body: 這才是資安工程師真正需要回答的問題

sourceBody.text: 注意：CVE、CWE、CPE 都不是駭客使用的攻擊工具，它們是讓研究人員、軟體廠商、資安工程師與弱點掃描器能交換資訊的共同語言。
二、CVE：每個公開漏洞的「案件編號」
CVE 全名是 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures，中文常稱「通用漏洞與曝險」。
你可以把它想成警察辦案時使用的案件識別編號。
假設某間軟體公司發現，自己的產品存在一個漏洞：
「未登入的使用者，在特定條件下可能讀取不應公開的文件。」
如果沒有共同編號，可能會出現：

items: A 廠商稱它為「文件外洩問題」。
B 掃描器稱它為「未授權讀取漏洞」。
C 研究員稱它為「權限驗證缺陷」。

sourceBody.text: 三個人可能在討論同一件事，但使用不同名稱。
CVE 就是用來降低這種混亂的。
CVE 編號怎麼看？

visual.caption: 圖 2｜CVE-2021-44228 編號結構
visual.description: 這是真實的 Log4Shell 編號；年份不是漏洞被發現或首次遭利用的必然日期。

items.title: CVE
items.body: 漏洞識別系統
編號年份
識別流水號

sourceBody.text: CVE 不會直接告訴你：

items: 你的電腦是否安裝了有問題的軟體。
你的軟體是否已經修補。
駭客是否已經利用這個漏洞。
漏洞的嚴重程度是多少。

sourceBody.text: 它的首要作用，是讓大家知道正在討論的是哪個漏洞。
CVE 也有不同狀態

rows: 編號先保留下來，細節可能還沒公布
這個編號已被判定不應繼續作為有效漏洞紀錄

sourceBody.text: 有些編號遭 Rejected，是因為重複登錄、紀錄有誤或其他原因。應查看原始說明及是否有替代編號。
還有一個專業名詞叫 CNA（CVE Numbering Authority），就是在指定範圍內負責分配及發布 CVE 紀錄的組織。你現在只需要知道：CVE 不是任何人隨意取一個數字就算成立。
[CVE 狀態與 CNA 說明](https://www.cve.org/Resources/Media/Archives/OldWebsite/about/faqs.html)
三、CWE：漏洞背後「犯了哪一類錯誤」
CWE 全名是 Common Weakness Enumeration，中文是「通用弱點列舉」。
假設你是修車師傅。
今天有三輛不同品牌的車，都出現煞車失靈。
三件召回事件各有自己的案件編號，但仔細調查之後，你發現三個問題都源於相似的設計缺陷。
這時候，三個不同的 CVE 就可能對應同一類 CWE。
以 CWE-79 為例：XSS 跨網站指令碼
想像你經營一個留言網站。
正常情況下，訪客留言：
今天的天氣很好。
網站就應該把它當成普通文字，顯示在畫面上。
但是某個網站沒有正確處理使用者輸入的內容，導致有人輸入的網頁程式碼，被其他訪客的瀏覽器當成指令執行。
這就可能形成 XSS（Cross-Site Scripting）。
問題的根源，不是留言功能本身，而是程式沒有妥善區分「使用者提供的資料」和「可以執行的網頁程式碼」。
MITRE 將這類缺陷整理為 CWE-79。
理解這個差異很有用：
CVE 主要幫你找到某次具體的漏洞及修補資訊；CWE 則能幫工程師思考如何從程式設計、輸出編碼、框架選擇及安全測試等層面，降低同類問題反覆發生的機率。
而且，不是每個 CWE 都一定對應某個 CVE。你自己開發的系統即使沒有公開 CVE，也可能存在 CWE 所描述的缺陷。
[MITRE CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html)
四、CPE：辨認「到底是哪個產品、哪個版本」
CPE 全名是 Common Platform Enumeration，中文是「通用平台列舉」。
我們再回到汽車的例子。
如果車廠宣布：
「2023 年生產的某款車型存在煞車問題。」
你總不能因為自己也是同一個品牌，就認為自己的車一定需要召回。
軟體也是如此。
假設某間公司使用三套不同版本的文件伺服器：
為了讓掃描器和資料庫能使用一致的方式描述產品，就需要 CPE。
CPE 長什麼樣子？
假設有一個虛構產品，叫做 Orange Document Server 2.4。
我們可以用教學用的 CPE 2.3 字串表示：
cpe:2.3:a:orange:document_server:2.4:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
你先認識最重要的部分：

items: `cpe:2.3`：CPE 命名格式版本。
`a`：Application，應用程式（`o` 是作業系統，`h` 是硬體）。
`orange`：廠商。
`document_server`：產品。

sourceBody.text: 後面的欄位還能描述更新、版本類型、語言及其他條件。完整格式不需要現在背下來。
有兩件事情要特別注意：
第一，CPE 不是設備身分證。 公司有十台電腦安裝相同版本的軟體，它們可能符合相同的 CPE，但仍然是十台不同設備。
第二，CPE 比對成功，不代表漏洞一定存在。 因為真正是否受影響，還可能取決於功能是否啟用、套件是否修補，以及其他軟體或平台條件。
[NIST CPE 2.3 命名規格](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ir/7695/final)
五、NVD：整合公開漏洞資訊的資料庫
前面認識了三種識別方式，但你可能會想：
「這麼多 CVE，我要到哪裡查？」
答案之一，就是 NVD。
NVD 全名是 National Vulnerability Database，美國國家漏洞資料庫，由 NIST 維護。
你可以把它想成一個資安資料整理中心。

visual.caption: 圖 3｜公開資料到現場查證
visual.description: 建議查證順序；資料完整度與更新先後需逐案核對。

items.title: CVE 官方紀錄
items.body: 這個漏洞是什麼？編號是否有效？有哪些參考資料？

items.title: NVD 補充分析
items.body: 可能受影響的產品條件、CWE 類型、CVSS 嚴重度等（視資料完整程度）

items.title: 廠商安全公告
items.body: 哪些版本真的受影響？有什麼限制？應更新到哪個版本？

items.title: 自己的系統與資產紀錄
items.body: 實際安裝版本、設定、修補狀態及執行中的元件

sourceBody.text: 上圖是建議的查證順序，不代表 NVD 必然完整，也不代表廠商公告一定比其他來源更新。
例如在真實的 [CVE-2021-44228 的 NVD 頁面](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228)，就能查到 Log4Shell 的描述、嚴重度、產品適用條件及相關公告。Apache 自己的安全公告還進一步說明，受影響的是 `log4j-core` 元件，不能把所有名稱中有 Log4j 的元件都當成同樣受影響。
為什麼不能只相信 NVD？
因為資料庫也需要時間整理資料。
NIST 在 2026 年 4 月 15 日宣布，NVD 改以風險為導向，優先補充已知遭利用漏洞、聯邦政府使用的軟體等紀錄。其他 CVE 仍會列入，但可能不會立即補上全部分析資訊。
所以，NVD 沒有顯示完整 CPE 或嚴重度資料，不等於漏洞不存在，也不代表風險是零。
[NIST 2026-04-15 NVD 政策](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/04/nist-updates-nvd-operations-address-record-cve-growth)
[Apache 安全公告](https://logging.apache.org/security.html)
六、完整模擬案例：掃描器告訴你「有漏洞」，你該怎麼做？
現在假設你是某公司的資安工程師。
公司有一台對外提供服務的文件伺服器。
弱點掃描器回報：

visual.caption: 圖 4｜掃描器發現：待確認
visual.description: 以下是虛構教學案例，不是真實掃描結果或 CVE。

items.title: 產品
items.body: Orange Document Server

items.title: 漏洞條件
items.body: 必須開啟文件預覽功能

sourceBody.text: 乍看之下，2.4 在受影響範圍內，你可能想直接在報告寫「已確認存在漏洞」。
但這樣太快了。
第一步：確認版本是不是真的
掃描器可能只是看到網站回應：
`Server: Orange Document Server 2.4`
這個文字不一定等於目前實際執行的完整軟體版本。它可能是舊資訊、被設定成固定值，或忽略了套件修訂號。
因此需要確認實際安裝的產品與套件版本，而不是只相信網站提供的字串。
第二步：確認漏洞成立的條件
公告指出：只有啟用「文件預覽」功能時才會受影響。
那就需要檢查設定。
如果功能沒有啟用，這條攻擊路徑可能不成立；但你還不能因此斷言整個產品絕對安全。
第三步：確認修補狀態
這裡要認識一個重要觀念：Backport，中文常稱「安全修補回移」。
假設某套軟體版本是 2.4，原廠後來將 2.7 的某個安全修補移植回 2.4 維護分支。
結果可能出現：

items: 版本看起來仍然是 2.4。
但套件已包含修正漏洞的程式碼。

sourceBody.text: 這不是理論上的例外。Linux 發行商確實會採取 Backport 策略，因此單看上游版本號可能造成掃描器誤報。
反過來說，系統管理員口頭表示「我們有更新」，也不是足夠證據。還需要確認實際安裝的完整套件版本、更新紀錄，必要時確認執行中的服務是否已載入更新。
第四步：依照證據下結論
現在把情況分成三種。

rows: 確認未修補、預覽功能也已開啟
符合已知漏洞成立條件，可判定受影響
確認已有對應修補，而且正在執行修補後版本
可認定該公告漏洞已修復，仍需記錄證據

sourceBody.text: 這三種結果的差異，就是資安工程師和單純操作掃描器的人最重要的能力差距。
[Red Hat 安全修補回移](https://access.redhat.com/security/updates/backporting)
七、寫資安報告時，怎麼區分證據的強度？
這裡有一個非常實用的觀念：發現弱點、確認弱點、證明可利用、確認已遭入侵，是四個不同層次。

visual.caption: 圖 5｜四種證據層次
visual.description: 教學層次不表示每項弱點都須利用測試，成功利用也不能證明過去遭入侵。

items.title: 發現疑似弱點（Potential Finding）
items.body: 掃描器比對到某個 CVE，表示值得調查，尚未確認適用條件。

items.title: 確認受到影響（Confirmed Vulnerability）
items.body: 有足夠證據確認產品、版本、設定與修補狀態符合漏洞成立條件。

items.title: 驗證實際可利用性（Validated Exploitability）
items.body: 在授權範圍內，以受控測試證明漏洞確實可以產生特定安全影響。

items.title: 發現實際入侵（Evidence of Compromise）
items.body: 透過日誌、鑑識等證據，確認曾發生未經授權的利用或入侵活動。

sourceBody.text: 這是一個方便教學的證據層次模型，不代表所有弱點都必須執行利用測試才能成立，也不表示單靠成功利用就能推論以前已有駭客入侵。
一份比較專業的弱點紀錄
沿用前面的虛構案例：

rows: 文件預覽功能的權限控制缺陷
教學公告，未使用真實編號
掃描器偵測為 2.4，尚待主機端確認
公告指出 2.4～2.6 且啟用預覽時受影響
預覽功能、修補與執行狀態
先完成版本與設定查核，再依結果修補或排除

sourceBody.text: 你在正式滲透測試報告裡，可以這樣寫：
經初步偵測，目標系統回應資訊與公開安全公告所列的受影響產品版本相符。然而，目前尚未完成實際套件版本、功能設定及修補狀態查核，亦未進行漏洞利用驗證。因此，本項列為疑似弱點，建議由系統維護單位進一步確認並提供相關證據。
這種寫法同時做到三件事：揭露安全疑慮、不誇大已取得的證據，以及清楚指定接下來要查什麼。
八、這一課的知識整理

rows: 這屬於哪類程式設計或系統缺陷？
可能影響哪些產品與版本？
哪裡可以查詢公開漏洞資訊？
廠商安全公告及修補說明
我的設備是否真的受影響？
資產、版本、設定及修補證據
事件紀錄、鑑識與入侵調查

sourceBody.text: 官方學習資源可由 [CVE 官方網站](https://www.cve.org/)、[MITRE CWE](https://cwe.mitre.org/)、[NVD 弱點資料庫](https://nvd.nist.gov/) 開始查閱。
九、理解檢核
假設你幫一間公司做弱點掃描，發現：
某台 Ubuntu 伺服器的 Nginx 被辨識為較舊版本。掃描器據此列出一個 CVE，評為高風險。
但系統管理員說：「我們已經透過 Ubuntu 的安全更新修補過了，只是 Nginx 主要版本號沒有變。」
請回答兩個問題：

items: 你應該直接相信掃描器，還是直接相信系統管理員？為什麼？
你會向系統管理員索取哪兩項關鍵證據，判斷這個漏洞是否真的已經修補？

sourceBody.text: 請先寫下你的判斷與所需證據，再於後續討論核對推理；本頁不提供自動送出或批改功能。
這一課最重要的一句話是：
CVE 告訴你要調查哪個漏洞，CWE 告訴你要理解哪類缺陷，CPE 幫你找出可能受影響的產品；但只有現場證據，才能讓你對這台設備做出可靠的判斷。

en.summary: Distinguish vulnerability identifiers, weakness types and product names; investigate scanner warnings using version, configuration and patch evidence.

sourceBody.text: This lesson helps you go beyond recognizing security terminology to judge whether a vulnerability scanner's warning actually applies to a system.
Start with one principle:
A scanner reporting a possible vulnerability does not establish that it exists on the system. Even a confirmed vulnerability does not establish that an attacker has compromised it.
1. Understand three terms through a vehicle recall
Suppose you bought a Toyota.
One day, a news report says a particular Toyota model has a brake-system defect and the manufacturer has announced a recall.
You would want to know:

items: Which recall incident is this?
What type of brake problem is involved?
Does it affect my model and production year?

sourceBody.text: Information security has three corresponding standards.

rows: Reference number for a recall incident
Identifier for a specific disclosed vulnerability
Type of brake design or manufacturing error
Type of weakness underlying a vulnerability
Standardized name for a software, hardware or operating-system product

visual.caption: Figure 1 | CVE, CWE, CPE and local evidence
visual.description: Three parallel perspectives jointly support a device applicability judgment.

items.title: CVE
items.body: Which vulnerability?

items.title: CWE
items.body: Which weakness type?

items.title: CPE
items.body: Which products may be affected?

items.title: Compare versions, settings, patches and local evidence
items.body: Check actual conditions using all three perspectives

items.title: Is this actual device affected?
items.body: This is the question the security engineer needs to answer

sourceBody.text: CVE, CWE and CPE are a common language for researchers, vendors, security engineers and scanners to exchange information. They are not attack tools.
2. CVE: a reference number for a disclosed vulnerability
CVE stands for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures.
Think of it as an identifier used to coordinate work on a particular case.
Suppose a software company discovers a vulnerability in its product:
Under certain conditions, an unauthenticated user may read documents that should not be public.
Without a common identifier, descriptions could differ:

items: Vendor A calls it a document-disclosure problem.
Scanner B calls it an unauthorized-read vulnerability.
Researcher C calls it an authorization-check flaw.

sourceBody.text: All three may be discussing the same issue under different names.
CVE helps reduce that confusion.
Reading a CVE identifier

visual.caption: Figure 2 | CVE-2021-44228 identifier structure
visual.description: This is the real Log4Shell identifier; its year does not necessarily indicate discovery or first exploitation.

items.title: CVE
items.body: Vulnerability identifier system
Identifier year
Sequence number

sourceBody.text: A CVE identifier does not directly tell you:

items: Whether the affected software is installed on your computer.
Whether your software has been patched.
Whether an attacker has exploited it.
How severe the vulnerability is.

sourceBody.text: Its primary role is to identify the vulnerability being discussed.
CVE record states

rows: An identifier has been reserved; details may not yet be public
The vulnerability record is publicly available
The identifier should no longer be treated as a valid vulnerability record

sourceBody.text: A record may be rejected because it duplicates another record, contains an error or for another reason. Read the explanation and any replacement identifier.
A CNA (CVE Numbering Authority) assigns identifiers and publishes records within its designated scope. A number chosen arbitrarily does not become an official CVE identifier.
[CVE states and CNA responsibilities](https://www.cve.org/Resources/Media/Archives/OldWebsite/about/faqs.html)
3. CWE: the type of mistake behind a vulnerability
CWE stands for Common Weakness Enumeration.
Imagine you are a vehicle mechanic.
Three cars from different manufacturers arrive with brake failures.
Each recall has its own reference number, but investigation reveals similar design defects.
Likewise, three different CVEs can map to the same CWE type.
CWE-79: cross-site scripting
Imagine running a website with a comments section.
A visitor normally posts:
The weather is nice today.
The website should display this as ordinary text.
If a website handles user input incorrectly, someone else's submitted web code may instead execute as instructions in another visitor's browser.
This can produce XSS (Cross-Site Scripting).
The underlying problem is a failure to distinguish user-supplied data from executable web code, rather than the existence of a comments feature itself.
MITRE classifies this weakness as CWE-79.
The distinction is useful:
CVE helps locate a specific vulnerability and its fixes. CWE helps engineers prevent recurring weakness types through design, output encoding, framework choices and security tests.
Not every CWE instance has a CVE. Your own application can contain a weakness described by CWE even without a publicly assigned vulnerability identifier.
[MITRE CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html)
4. CPE: identify the product and version
CPE stands for Common Platform Enumeration.
Return to the vehicle analogy.
Suppose a manufacturer announces:
A particular model produced in 2023 has a brake problem.
Owning another vehicle from the same brand does not establish that it is included in the recall.
Software requires the same distinction.
Suppose a company runs three document-server versions:
CPE gives scanners and databases a consistent way to describe products.
What does CPE look like?
Consider a fictional product named Orange Document Server 2.4.
A teaching example using the CPE 2.3 format is:
cpe:2.3:a:orange:document_server:2.4:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
Start with the main fields:

items: `cpe:2.3`: version of the CPE naming format.
`a`: application; `o` denotes an operating system and `h` hardware.
`orange`: vendor.
`document_server`: product.
`2.4`: version.

sourceBody.text: Later fields can describe updates, editions, language and other conditions. You do not need to memorize the entire format now.
Two distinctions matter:
First, CPE is not a device identity. Ten computers running the same software version can match one CPE while remaining ten different assets.
Second, a CPE match does not establish vulnerability applicability. Enabled features, installed patches and other software or platform conditions may determine whether the asset is affected.
[NIST CPE 2.3 naming specification](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ir/7695/final)
5. NVD: a database integrating public vulnerability information
After learning three identifiers, you may ask:
Where can I look up all these CVEs?
One option is NVD.
NVD stands for National Vulnerability Database, maintained by NIST in the United States.
Think of it as a center for organizing vulnerability information.

visual.caption: Figure 3 | From public records to local verification
visual.description: Suggested investigation order; verify completeness and freshness for each case.

items.title: Official CVE record
items.body: What is it? Is the ID valid? Which references are available?

items.title: NVD enrichment
items.body: Affected product conditions, CWE types and CVSS severity, depending on completeness

items.title: Vendor advisory
items.body: Which versions are affected? What conditions apply? Which update is needed?

items.title: Local system and asset records
items.body: Installed versions, configuration, patch status and running components

sourceBody.text: The illustration suggests an investigation order. It does not establish that NVD is always complete or that vendor advisories are always newer than other sources.

The real [NVD record for CVE-2021-44228](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228), for example, provides a Log4Shell description, severity information, applicability conditions and references. Apache's advisory further identifies `log4j-core` as the affected component; do not treat every component with Log4j in its name as equally affected.
Why consult sources beyond NVD?
Database enrichment takes time.

On April 15, 2026, NIST announced a risk-based approach prioritizing enrichment for categories including known exploited vulnerabilities and software used by the federal government. Other CVEs remain listed but may not immediately receive complete analysis.
Missing CPE or severity information in NVD therefore does not establish that the vulnerability is absent or its risk is zero.
[NIST NVD policy, April 15, 2026](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/04/nist-updates-nvd-operations-address-record-cve-growth)
[Apache security advisories](https://logging.apache.org/security.html)
6. Worked simulation: investigate a scanner warning
Suppose you are a company's security engineer.
The company operates an internet-facing document server.
A vulnerability scanner reports:

visual.caption: Figure 4 | Scanner finding: pending verification
visual.description: Fictional teaching case, not a real scan result or CVE.

items.title: Product
items.body: Orange Document Server

items.title: Vulnerability condition
items.body: Document preview must be enabled

sourceBody.text: Since 2.4 falls within the affected range, you might initially want to write “vulnerability confirmed.”
More evidence is needed first.
Step 1: verify the actual version
The scanner may have seen only this response:
`Server: Orange Document Server 2.4`
That string may be stale, configured as a fixed value or missing the package revision. It need not identify the complete version actually running.
Check the installed product and full package version as well as the response banner.
Step 2: verify the vulnerability conditions
The advisory says the issue applies only when document preview is enabled.
Check the configuration.
If the feature is disabled, this attack path may not apply. That still does not establish that the entire product is free of security problems.
Step 3: verify patch status
An important concept is backporting a security fix.
Suppose software is version 2.4 and the vendor later transfers a security fix from 2.7 into the maintained 2.4 branch.
The resulting situation can be:

items: The visible version still looks like 2.4.
The package contains the vulnerability fix.

sourceBody.text: Linux distributors use backporting in practice. Comparing upstream version numbers alone can therefore produce scanner false positives.

Conversely, an administrator saying “we updated it” is not sufficient evidence. Check the full installed package version, update records and, where necessary, whether the running service has loaded the update.
Step 4: conclude from the evidence
Distinguish three cases.

rows: Only the scanner's detected 2.4 version is known
Unpatched software and enabled preview are confirmed
Known applicability conditions are met; affected
The applicable fix is installed and the patched version is running
This advisory's vulnerability is fixed; retain the evidence

sourceBody.text: Distinguishing these outcomes is a central skill in engineering a vulnerability assessment.
[Red Hat security backporting](https://access.redhat.com/security/updates/backporting)
7. Report the strength of your evidence
Finding a possible vulnerability, confirming it, demonstrating exploitability and establishing compromise are four distinct evidence levels.

visual.caption: Figure 5 | Four evidence levels
visual.description: These teaching levels do not require exploitation for every finding, nor establish prior compromise from a successful test.

items.title: Potential Finding
items.body: A scanner match merits investigation; applicability remains unconfirmed.

items.title: Confirmed Vulnerability
items.body: Sufficient product, version, configuration and patch evidence establishes applicability.

items.title: Validated Exploitability
items.body: An authorized, controlled test demonstrates a specific security impact.

items.title: Evidence of Compromise
items.body: Logs or forensic evidence establish unauthorized exploitation or intrusion.

sourceBody.text: This teaching model does not require exploit testing to establish every vulnerability. A successful authorized test also does not prove that attackers exploited the issue previously.
A professional vulnerability record
Continue the fictional case:

rows: Teaching advisory; no real identifier assigned
Preview configuration, patches and running state
Verify versions and configuration, then remediate or exclude according to evidence

sourceBody.text: A penetration-testing report could say:

Preliminary detection found response information matching an affected product version in a public security advisory. Actual package versions, feature configuration and patch status have not yet been verified, and no exploitation test has been performed. This is therefore recorded as a potential vulnerability. The system maintenance team should verify these conditions and provide supporting evidence.
This discloses the concern, preserves the strength of the evidence and identifies what needs to be checked next.
8. Knowledge review

rows: Which design or system weakness type is involved?
Which products and versions may be affected?
Where can public vulnerability information be found?
Asset, version, configuration and patch evidence
Incident records, forensics and compromise investigation

sourceBody.text: Start with the [official CVE website](https://www.cve.org/), [MITRE CWE](https://cwe.mitre.org/) and [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/).
9. Understanding check
Suppose you scan a company's systems and observe:
An Ubuntu server's Nginx is identified as an older version. The scanner maps it to a CVE and rates it high risk.
The administrator says: “We applied Ubuntu security updates. The main Nginx version number just did not change.”
Answer two questions:

items: Should you immediately trust the scanner or the administrator? Why?
Which two key pieces of evidence would you request to determine whether this vulnerability has been patched?

sourceBody.text: Write your judgment and required evidence first, then review the reasoning in a subsequent discussion. This page provides no automatic submission or grading.
The lesson's central point is:
CVE identifies the vulnerability to investigate, CWE the weakness to understand, and CPE the products that may be affected. Local evidence supports a reliable judgment about this particular asset.
